subject: AdTechCo evaluation: tooling parity & next validation steps
messages:
From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@adtechco.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@adtechco.com
Date: 2026-12-10T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's demo — observability & procurement

Thanks Aditya — great demo today. A couple of things to make sure we can move this forward from our side:

- Observability parity: our infra team needs to understand how Redwood's telemetry maps to the fields we currently get from our hyperscaler endpoints (trace ids, span sampling, token-level cost attribution). Can you provide a short matrix or mapping?
- Live traces: we want a short proof that Redwood traces can be ingested into our Datadog workspace (or exported as OTLP).
- Latency profile: request a p50/p95/p99 summary for dynamic batching at 1–10 QPS with 256-token average prompts.
- Procurement: please loop in any standard SOW/PO process docs so our procurement lead (procurement@adtechco.com) can see timelines and payment terms.

If you can send a quick recap and proposed next tests, we can lock a follow-up call early next week.

—Mike
Head of ML Platforms, AdTechCo

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@adtechco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@adtechco.com
Date: 2026-12-10T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo — observability & procurement

Mike — thanks for the clear list. Recap below and proposed next steps. Attaching a short evaluation checklist and example traces.

Recap / Redwood signals and short answers:
- Telemetry mapping: we expose request_id, trace_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, inference_time_ms, and cost_estimate_per_request. We'll attach a parity matrix mapping these to the typical hyperscaler fields.
- Trace export: Redwood can emit OTLP and also push to Datadog via an OTLP->Datadog exporter. Laura will share a small ndjson trace sample you can ingest.
- Latency profile: baseline p50/p95/p99 numbers depend on model variant and quantization; for a mixed 13B open model under our dynamic-batching profile at 1–10 QPS with 256-token prompts we typically see p50 ~ 25–40ms/token, p95 ~ 120–180ms/token, p99 ~ 300–450ms/token. We'll run a benchmark using your exact prompt set to provide concrete numbers.
- Procurement / SOW: we have a standard SOW template and procurement checklist; copying procurement here.

Proposed next validation tests (can run in a 2–4 hour window):
1) Trace ingestion test — Redwood sends OTLP/traces for a 30-minute synthetic load; AdTechCo validates ingestion into Datadog (Deliverable: sample traces + ingestion confirmation).
2) Latency head-to-head — we run your 256-token prompt set against Redwood and your current hyperscaler endpoint with identical instance class where possible (Deliverable: p50/p95/p99 CSV + raw logs).
3) Cost attribution sanity check — run 1k requests and verify token-level cost fields reconcile with expected billing.
4) Dashboard parity review — Redwood will surface a short dashboard with token breakdowns and per-route traces; AdTechCo will confirm fields needed for the SRE team.

Next meetings:
- Proposed: Tue 2026-12-14 10:00 PT — 45 minutes (trace ingestion + bench plan). Laura and Marissa will join for technical coordination.

Attachments: adtech_evaluation_checklist.pdf, sample_traces.ndjson

Thanks — we'll prepare the bench harness and a runbook for the trace test.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo — observability & procurement

Adding a couple of operational details we should include in the runbook so AdTech's SRE has everything in one place:

- OTLP fields we'll export: trace_id, span_id, parent_id, service.name, http.status_code, model.name, model.version, batch_size, tokens.request, tokens.response, latency.ms. We'll include a short JSON example in the Drive doc.
- Authentication: for the short proof we'll provision a temporary API key scoped to tracing + read-only logs; the key will auto-expire after 48 hours.
- Environment parity: please confirm the hyperscaler instance type they're using; we'll try to match CPU/GPU class for a fair comparison. If they can't share exact instance, we'll use the closest Redwood Dedicated configuration.
- Success criteria for trace test: 95% of spans show model.name and batch_size; Datadog ingestion shows traces within 60s of export.

Action items (internal):
- Laura: prep the ndjson sample and an OTLP export guide (ETA EOD Mon 12/13).
- Aditya: confirm the Tue 12/14 slot and send calendar invite with call objectives.
- Marissa: prepare the bench harness config (256-token prompt set + burst pattern).

I'll put the runbook in Drive and share the link in the invite.

-Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
